clue.text: Group Leo formed for preliminary act

indicators.note: something formed is shaped from raw material, so the letters before it are moulded into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A band called Leo is put together to play as the warm-up act.
explanation.definitionFit: A prologue is an introductory section or performance that comes before the main work.

clue.text: Ms Honeyford's halo?

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name of the TV presenter ... Hunniford, spelt playfully here
second meaning: in art, a radiance surrounding a holy figure's head

explanation.walkthrough: Gloria Hunniford is a Northern Irish broadcaster well known on British television; the setter's spelling turns her surname into honey. The possessive just joins her name to the second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloria is a halo or aureole painted round a saint, and it is also the presenter's given name.

clue.text: Introduces quietly, but bears a grudge

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to resent something is to bear a grudge about it

explanation.surface: Someone makes polite introductions in a soft voice while secretly nursing resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone is to introduce them formally, as a host or compère does.

clue.text: Girl speaks of stars

indicators.note: speaks tells us to say the following word out loud and listen for a match

blocks.note: of the stars, and said aloud it matches the girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman talks about the night sky, or about celebrities.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a female given name, from the Latin word for star.

clue.text: Perhaps scholar has no aspiration to compose songs

indicators.note: aspiration is the breathy sound of the letter H, so having none means that letter is dropped
to compose is to put together or arrange, so the remaining letters are set in a new order

blocks.note: surface padding, softening the picture of the academic
taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic with no ambition might still try writing music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspiration' looks like ambition but is the phonetic term for an H sound; 'Perhaps' just softens the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Carols are songs, especially joyful religious ones sung at Christmas.

clue.text: Accountant to lend new illumination

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters before are rearranged

blocks.note: CA is a chartered accountant
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A finance professional offers to shed fresh light on matters.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle is a wax source of light, so it gives illumination.

clue.text: Old king with German name found in cave

blocks.note: GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George, as on old postboxes
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A historical German-named monarch is discovered hiding in a cavern.
explanation.definitionFit: A grotto is a small picturesque cave, natural or artificial.

clue.text: Business function

blocks.note: first meaning: a firm's workplace or bureau
second meaning: a duty or role someone holds

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about what a business does, but the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a place of work, and also a position or duty, as in the office of mayor.

clue.text: Best wishes for Christmas?

blocks.note: surface reading: a greeting written in a card
setter's reading: the two blessings traditionally wished for the season

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is a loose description rather than a synonym: a seasonal greeting phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Cards and carols commonly wish tranquillity and happiness to all at Christmas, so the phrase stands for festive greetings.

clue.text: Learnt about one of Rudolph's features

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters are turned into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has studied the anatomy of Father Christmas's famous reindeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolph is a reindeer, and reindeer grow branched horns on their heads.

clue.text: Simple, organised file for a comfortable existence

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters next to it are arranged afresh

blocks.note: simple and easy are synonyms
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A neat, tidy filing system makes office life comfortable.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy life is one free of hardship or effort, a relaxed and comfortable way of living.

clue.text: Good to pull a cork and hear this!

definitions.text: Good to pull a cork and hear this!

blocks.note: G is the standard abbreviation for good
to lug is to pull or drag something heavy

explanation.surface: A wine lover says it is good to draw the cork and hear the first pour.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the sound of wine pouring from a newly opened bottle, while its first words also build the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Glug is the gurgling noise liquid makes when poured from a bottle, a welcome sound once the cork is drawn.

clue.text: One scene, shortened before the ballet, has superior power

indicators.note: shortened means cut down, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a means one
taken as written before trimming
ballet is a form of dance

explanation.surface: A cut-down scene staged ahead of the ballet carries great dramatic force.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascendance is dominance or controlling influence over others, the state of having the upper hand.

clue.text: Worried? Anyway, see doctor at the beginning of January

indicators.note: worried can mean shaken about, as a dog worries a bone, so the letters are tossed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

explanation.surface: An anxious person is told to visit a GP after the holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of January is the opening day of the calendar year, a public holiday.

clue.text: Diet madly after Christmas season

indicators.note: madly means wildly, so the letters next to it are scrambled

blocks.note: Yule is an old name for Christmas
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: People frantically go on diets once the festive season ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Christmas season' looks like one phrase defining the answer, but Christmas is wordplay and only 'season' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the Christmas period, a time of year, so it is a season.

clue.text: Responded to desperate war needs …

indicators.note: desperate suggests frantic and disordered, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone reacted to the urgent requirements of a wartime nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To have answered is to have replied or reacted, a direct synonym for responded.

clue.text: … at one point supplied weapons that heightened temperature

blocks.note: W, west, is one point of the compass
to arm is to supply with weapons

explanation.surface: Continuing the war theme: at some stage the arms supply made things hotter.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 15 down; 'at' here only carries on that sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Warmed is a past-tense verb meaning made hotter, so it matches raising the temperature.

clue.text: Fly around, aim to move tribe

indicators.note: around suggests turning things about, so the letters are reordered
moving letters means shifting their positions into a new sequence

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Travel by plane with the intention of relocating your whole clan.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a group of related people, and family is used loosely for the same kinship group.

clue.text: One lapses into bad habits, but supports cover with some hesitation

blocks.note: to back is to support
a lid is a cover
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone slipping into old vices still hesitantly defends and covers for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A backslider is a person who relapses into former sins or bad behaviour after reforming.

clue.text: Rickety rickshaw dropping final couple for a drink

indicators.note: dropping the final couple means losing the last two letters of the word
rickety means shaky and falling apart, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A wobbly rickshaw sheds a couple of passengers on the way to the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Kirsch is a clear brandy distilled from cherries, a spirit you drink.

clue.text: Such wit is double-edged

blocks.note: surface reading: a type of sharp, cutting humour
setter's reading: the slender sword that names that humour has two cutting edges

explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on the phrase for very quick, cutting humour and on the blade itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase rapier wit means sharp repartee, named after a thin sword with a keen edge.

clue.text: One of the glitterati, originally from Surbiton, taking a rest

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of each word, its opening letter

blocks.note: the initial letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A celebrity from a London suburb is having a break.
explanation.walkthrough: Surbiton is a suburb in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: The glitterati are fashionable celebrities, and a star is a famous performer among them.

clue.text: One more races round for cupid

blocks.note: a means one
taken as written
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone runs another lap in search of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'races round' looks like an anagram or container instruction, but both words supply letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An amoretto is a cherub representing Cupid in Renaissance art, a little love god.

clue.text: Lyrical writer of macabre stories has a twitch

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote tales of horror
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A horror author suffers from a nervous spasm.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetic describes expressive, song-like language, so it is a synonym of lyrical.

clue.text: Month I'd get last chance to make a choice

indicators.note: last tells us to keep only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
taken as written without the apostrophe
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: In December someone is given a final opportunity to choose.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide is to settle on an option, which is what making a choice means.

clue.text: Cure found for some extreme dysfunctions

indicators.note: some means only a part, so the letters lie inside the words that follow

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A treatment has been discovered for certain severe disorders.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is a treatment that heals, so it is a synonym of cure.
